newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Texaco official's hearing delayed due to talks.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Texaco official's hearing delayed due to talks.

text.p: A preliminary hearing in the case of a former Texaco Inc. executive charged with obstruction of justice in a racial discrimination case has been delayed while prosecutors negotiate with his lawyer, according to court papers released Tuesday.

According to the documents, the delay was sought by the government in the case of Richard Lundwall because his lawyer was in talks with the government on certain issues "including the possible disposition of the case without trial."
A spokesman for the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York would not comment further.
The preliminary hearing in the case had been set for Wednesday, but a White Plains, N.Y., magistrate judge signed an order on Monday granting a 30-day continuance until Jan. 15.

Last month Lundwall, 55, of Danbury, Conn. was charged in a one-count complaint filed by prosecutors. At the time, legal experts speculated that he had been charged by complaint instead of a grand jury indictment in anticipation a plea and that a cooperation agreement could be reached.
So far Lundwall is the only individual who has been charged by the federal government with obstruction of justice stemming from the discrimination case.

Lundwall, former senior coordinator of personnel services of Texaco's finance department, had made secret tapes of himself and other Texaco officers discussing the destruction of documents in a racial discrimination case.
After being forced out of the company, Lundwall turned over the tapes to plaintiffs lawyers in that suit.
Transcripts of the tapes, which included racist remarks, were made public as part of the court record in the discrimation case. Publicity over the tapes generated wide-spread outrage and protests.
Last month company agreed to settle the case last month by paying $176.1 million and establishing an "equality and tolerance" task force.
